ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure 1 shows a circle inscribed in a square, touching the square on all four sides. Figure 2 shows three congruent circles lined up horizontally, with adjacent circles tangent to each other. Reasoning: Let the radius of each circle be r. Since the circle in Figure 1 is inscribed in the square, the square side length is 2r, so its area is a = (2r)^2 = 4r^2. Each circle has area b = πr^2. In Figure 2, a taut elastic band around the three tangent circles forms a stadium-shaped boundary: a rectangle of length 4r between the centers of the two outer circles and height 2r, plus two semicircular end caps. The rectangle area is 4r · 2r = 8r^2 = 2a. The two semicircular end caps together equal one full circle, with area b. Therefore, the total area inside the elastic band is 2a + b.

method.method_draft: Read Figure 1 as a circle inscribed in a square, so if the circle radius is r, the square side is 2r. From the text, the square area is a, so a = 4r^2, and each circle area is b = pi r^2. Read Figure 2 as three congruent circles tangent in a horizontal row. A taut elastic band around them forms a stadium-shaped convex hull: a rectangle between the centers of the two outer circles, of length 4r and height 2r, plus two semicircular end caps that together make one full circle. The rectangle area is 4r * 2r = 8r^2 = 2a, and the two semicircles have total area b. Therefore the banded area is 2a + b.

method.method_draft: Read Figure 1 as giving a reference square whose side equals one circle diameter; hence any diameter-square around one of the circles has area a, while the circle itself has area b. In Figure 2, imagine the smallest rectangle aligned with the three horizontally tangent circles. This rectangle consists of three adjacent diameter-squares, so its area is 3a. The elastic band region fills this rectangle except for the four corner pieces at the far left and far right, outside the rounded end arcs. Those four missing corner pieces are exactly equivalent to the area of one diameter-square outside its inscribed circle, namely a - b: half of that difference is missing at the left end and half at the right end. Thus the banded area is 3a - (a - b) = 2a + b.
